answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to prove ongoing work by completing a challenge-bound chain of sequential modular squarings, with each result needed to compute the next. GPUs can accelerate individual operations, but cannot parallelize steps within a chain; multiple clones therefore demand separate serial chains and impose a real time cost, not a free increase in identities. Wesolowski proofs let verifiers check completion efficiently, keeping the basalt ledge below the zenith of attacker throughput.
